review_conclusion: Accept EXP-006 correctness, arithmetic/count and scoped normal-assembly gate for a fresh EXP-005/EXP-006 timing comparison; no performance or leakage-resistance conclusion yet.
correctness_findings: Twelve normal/UBSan builds pass the 45/53/61-vector dot oracle, coefficient bounds, four error-addition patterns, final reduction and polynomial serialization checks.
All four 100-fixture KEM transcripts per parameter match exactly; malformed secret keys, corrupted/random ciphertexts and noncanonical public keys are covered by the shared fixtures.
All three upstream suites pass and all ninety count observations reproduce the expected summaries.
Baseline source matches pinned upstream; candidate is exactly the three proposed source edits, with the other 32 files matching accepted EXP-005.
Bounds/scale preserve final centred public-key bytes while keeping general dot and inverse-input contracts intact. Sampled tests and UBSan do not replace the conditional range argument.
assembly_findings: New keygen dot bodies are identical to the preserved general dot after function-symbol renaming except the final tail jump: poly_reduce becomes poly_tomont. The stack frame is restored before that jump.

New dot bodies have 285/355/413 bytes, 24-byte local reservations plus 48 bytes of saved registers, no local canary and endbr64. Their branches use public pair parity and fixed 128-pair termination; component arithmetic is unrolled.

The general dot, poly_tomont and both reducers match EXP-005 normalised bodies. poly_tomont retains 256 fixed-index Montgomery conversions with multiplier 1353; reducers have no division or conditional branches.

Keygen calls only the dedicated dot for the changed matrix loop; skpv forward reduction, direct error NTT, final addition/reduction and serialization remain. Kyber512 and Kyber768 use K unrolled calls; Kyber1024 retains a public four-row loop.

Keygen body size changes 442->423, 512->521, 988->980 bytes. The sum of keygen plus newly added dot bodies grows by 266/364/405 bytes; this is a scoped function-size sum, not total ELF text or instruction-cache cost.
Keygen local stack including saved registers changes 5272->5272, 9384->9368, 15032->15032 bytes, excluding entry return address/callees. Canary checks, endbr64 and one/two/three page probes remain.
Kyber1024 retains public-matrix rejection sampling, so the whole keygen routine is not described as branchless or independent of every public input.
security_findings: No new secret-coefficient-dependent control/address selection is observed in the reviewed changed path. This is a scoped source/generated-code finding, not whole-program constant-time proof.

The general dot already lacks a local canary following EXP-002; EXP-006 preserves it and adds a second function with the same local hardening pattern. No protection flag is disabled and keygen canaries remain.
Larger representatives, code duplication, call scheduling and layout can affect properties not measured by counts. Exact signed-conversion/right-shift assumptions remain compiler/target-specific.

Statistical timing leakage and dynamic secret-flow testing remain not-run and required before the final security assessment. Physical power/EM/fault behaviour, exhaustive memory safety and final ML-KEM conformance remain unestablished.
VTune is excluded from the remaining plan at the user's request; this does not remove the required focused security assessment.
review_method: Read SHA-1-verified loose Git objects without Git commands; verify retained artifacts and commands; compare transcripts and counts; re-extract normal bodies from verified executables with recorded objdump, cross-check sizes with nm, and inspect instructions/control flow. No arithmetic edit, full validation rerun or primary timing run.
